name: Spare Construct
replaces: Revit, and the add-ins people buy or bolt on to it: Navisworks, Revizto and BIMcollab for clash; Solibri and UpCodes for model checking; Enscape, Twinmotion, Lumion and D5 Render for rendering; Dynamo for visual scripting; pyRevit, DiRoots, Ideate and Naviate toolkits; Ideate BIMLink and DiRoots SheetLink for Excel; AGACAD, StrucSoft MWF and hsbcad for framing; CostX and Assemble for quantities; Autodesk Docs, Newforma and Aconex for document control
summary: One open building model for every discipline, built from scratch in Rust, that runs on the desktop, in the browser and headless for AI and scripts. Everything people buy add-ins for today is built in as first-party add-ins on the same public API, free to use, with hosting run at cost.

areas.name: Getting started, accounts and settings
areas.summary: How a person finds, installs and starts Spare Construct, signs in only when they need to, sets preferences and learns the tool. No licence keys and no paywall.

features.name: Download and install
features.does: Install Spare Construct on Windows, macOS or Linux, or open it in a browser, with no licence key.

parts.name: Desktop installers
parts.what: Signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux built from the desktop shell, signed through the kit's release signing (KIT-A22-F2-P3).

parts.name: Hardware check
parts.what: Checks the graphics card, memory and browser support on first run and explains any limit in plain words.

parts.name: Browser start
parts.what: Opens the app in a browser with the core in a web worker and the cross-origin headers that threads need.

parts.name: Offline installers
parts.what: Full installers an office can copy to machines with no internet, with the help library and starter content included.

features.name: Sign in, or work without an account
features.does: Use the desktop app fully offline with no account, and sign in only to share, sync or publish.

parts.name: Spareware sign-in
parts.what: One Spareware login, passkey first, through the kit's account service (KIT-A1-F1-P1, KIT-A1-F2-P1), used only for sharing and hosted features.

parts.name: Local profile
parts.what: A local profile that holds preferences and recent projects with no account at all.

features.name: Start a first project
features.does: Create a project from a template for their country and project type, or open a sample, in under a minute.

parts.name: New project flow
parts.what: Picks country, units, template and project location, then opens the first view.

parts.name: Starter templates
parts.what: Open templates per country and discipline: levels, view types, title blocks, parameters and styles.

parts.name: Sample projects
parts.what: A house, a small commercial building and a multi-storey building to learn and test with.

parts.name: Home screen
parts.what: Recent projects, pinned projects, templates and learning links on one start page.

features.name: Bring my old work across
features.does: Move from Revit by bringing models, families, templates and office standards across in one guided step.

parts.name: Move from Revit guide
parts.what: A guided import that takes exported models, parameter lists and office standards and maps them to Spare Construct.

parts.name: Standards mapper
parts.what: Maps categories, line styles, fill patterns and parameter names to ours and reports what did not map.

parts.name: Move report
parts.what: A plain report of what came across, what changed and what needs a person to check.

features.name: Learn as I go
features.does: Learn the tool through short lessons, tips in context and searchable help, with no paid training needed.

parts.name: Help library
parts.what: Searchable help pages for every command, generated from the command schema plus written guides, and published through the kit's help centre (KIT-A21-F1-P1). The same source builds the public documentation site (A24-F5-P2).

parts.name: Interactive lessons
parts.what: Step-by-step lessons that run inside a sample project and check each step.

parts.name: Tips in context
parts.what: Short hints on the first use of a tool, which can be turned off.

parts.name: Revit terms finder
parts.what: Type a Revit term and find the matching Spare Construct command or idea.

parts.name: Offline help
parts.what: The help library and lessons installed with the app, so help works with no connection.

features.name: Set my preferences
features.does: Set units, snaps, shortcuts, colours, language and file locations once and carry them to every computer.

parts.name: Preferences store
parts.what: Typed preferences per person, per office and per project, with a clear order of precedence.

parts.name: Preference sync
parts.what: Carries a signed-in person's Spare Construct preferences to every device through the kit's settings (KIT-A20-F5-P1) and sync (KIT-A15-F4-P2).

parts.name: Shortcut editor
parts.what: Rebind any command to keys or a two-key sequence, and import an existing keyboard file.

features.name: Get help when stuck
features.does: Report a problem, see known issues and service status, get support as a paying office, and get an answer from the community or an AI helper.

parts.name: Problem report
parts.what: Sends a report with the log, the operations leading up to it and an optional anonymised piece of model, only with consent, through the kit's crash reports (KIT-A22-F9-P1). Report storage is metered so its cost reaches the ledger (KIT-A13-F2-P2).

parts.name: Crash recovery
parts.what: Reopens after a crash with every operation up to the crash replayed.

parts.name: AI helper
parts.what: One in-app AI helper, built on the kit's help assistant (KIT-A17-F7-P1). It answers how-to questions from the help library and, when asked, proposes commands the person sees before they run. It replaces the separate in-app assistant that was CON-A19-F3-P3.

parts.name: Support for paying offices
parts.what: Support cases for offices that pay for hosting, through the kit's support cases (KIT-A21-F2-P1), with the project and version attached when the office agrees.

parts.name: Service status
parts.what: Hosted sync, library and sharing shown on the kit's status page (KIT-A21-F5-P1), linked from the app.

parts.name: AI choice and project data
parts.what: Spare Construct's rule on what model and client data an in-app AI may receive, set by the office per project. Choosing the model and paying at cost follow the kit's AI tools policy (KIT-A17-F6-P1). Next, with the AI helper, because the first release sends nothing to a co-op AI.

features.name: Sign in with my office's own login
features.does: Sign in to Spare Construct through an office's own identity provider, as a member of the office's team.

parts.name: Office sign-in
parts.what: Sign in through an office's own identity provider, as a member of the office's organisation, using the kit's organisation model (KIT-A1-F7-P1) and outside sign-in links (KIT-A1-F10-P1). Later, not core, because both kit parts come after the kit's first release.

features.name: Stay up to date on my chosen channel
features.does: Get updates in the background on a stable, preview or pinned channel, and roll back if a release causes trouble.

parts.name: Updates and channels
parts.what: Spare Construct's update rules (stable, preview and pinned channels, versions pinned per project, and roll back) delivered through the kit's update delivery (KIT-A20-F7-P1) and signed releases (KIT-A22-F2-P3), with update packages an office can copy to machines with no internet. Next, not core, because the kit's update delivery is next; the first release ships signed installers only.

areas.name: Model core, storage and speed
areas.summary: The database every element lives in, the project file, the operation log behind undo and sync, and the speed and truth tests that keep it fast and correct.

features.name: Keep the whole building in one model
features.does: Model architecture, structure and services in one model rather than a stack of linked files.

parts.name: Element store
parts.what: A column-by-column element store for millions of elements, with types stored once and instances storing only what differs.

parts.name: Permanent IDs
parts.what: 128-bit time-ordered IDs on disk and over the wire, with a compact index in memory, so offline work never collides.

parts.name: Relationship tables
parts.what: Hosted by, joined to, bounded by, in room, on level and in group, stored as tables and queryable both ways.

parts.name: Discipline ownership
parts.what: Every element has an owning discipline that views, permissions and exports can filter on.

features.name: Give elements data
features.does: Give any element typed parameters, formulas, shared parameters and project-wide values.

parts.name: Typed parameters
parts.what: Length, area, volume, angle, number, text, yes or no, choice, element link, material and web link values.

parts.name: Formula language
parts.what: A small, safe expression language for parameter formulas, with units checked.

parts.name: Shared parameters
parts.what: Parameters keyed by GUID so they match across projects, families and schedules.

parts.name: Project-wide values
parts.what: Named values that drive dimensions and parameters across the whole project.

parts.name: Project information
parts.what: Client, address, project number, stage and other project data that title blocks and exports read.

features.name: Work in real units and real places
features.does: Model in metres or feet with survey-accurate coordinates and true north.

parts.name: Units and display
parts.what: SI units inside in f64, with display units, rounding and formats as view and project settings.

parts.name: Coordinates and survey points
parts.what: Local building origin, project base point, survey point, true north and NZTM or any other projected system.

parts.name: Coordinate systems
parts.what: Coordinate system definitions and transforms for any country, from a database whose terms are checked first (A24-F1-P7). A candidate for the kit's maps, since other apps place things on maps too.

parts.name: Vertical datums
parts.what: NZVD2016 and the older local vertical datums, with the published transforms between them. Every level, spot height and drainage invert states its datum, so survey, flood and drainage levels line up.

features.name: Save and reopen without waiting
features.does: Save instantly and reopen a large project to its first view in seconds.

parts.name: Project file
parts.what: One portable project file holding chunk blobs, the operation log and the index, on the kit's chunked storage (KIT-A15-F6-P2), which Spare Construct needs in its first release.

parts.name: Chunked storage
parts.what: Elements grouped by building, level and spatial cell, compressed and content-hashed so unchanged chunks are never re-saved. Spare Construct needs the kit's chunked storage (KIT-A15-F6-P2, piece A06) in its first release, so it asks the kit to make that part core.

parts.name: Paging from disk
parts.what: Keeps recently used chunks in memory and pages the rest, so a city never has to fit in memory.

parts.name: Spatial index
parts.what: A bounding-volume hierarchy over chunks and elements that answers what is in a view or box in microseconds.

parts.name: Never-blocking save
parts.what: Operations append to the log at once and chunks compact in the background.

parts.name: Published file format
parts.what: A documented, versioned schema and a standalone reader library in Rust and Python, so files outlive the app.

parts.name: No forced upgrades
parts.what: Files open in older and newer releases without a one-way upgrade, using schema versions and migrations.

parts.name: Storage layout decision
parts.what: A decision note on chunks by building, level and cell or one flat file, the cell size, and levels or pure 3D cells. One of the six decisions that gate the Design stage; it has no work-board piece yet.

features.name: Undo anything
features.does: Undo and redo any change, including big batch changes, in one step.

parts.name: Operation log
parts.what: Every change is an operation in one log that drives undo, history and sync.

parts.name: Transactions
parts.what: Every command fully applies or fully rolls back.

parts.name: Undo and redo
parts.what: Steps through the operation log, grouped the way a person thinks of the change.

features.name: See edits update at once
features.does: Change one thing and see everything that depends on it update straight away, using every CPU core.

parts.name: Regeneration graph
parts.what: Incremental recomputation of only what changed, with early cut-off when a value comes out the same.

parts.name: Parallel rebuild
parts.what: Independent changed elements rebuild at the same time on a work-stealing thread pool.

parts.name: Progress and cancel
parts.what: Long global edits show progress and can be cancelled without harm.

features.name: See problems without being stopped
features.does: See modelling problems as a list linked to the elements, never as a dialog that stops work.

parts.name: Warnings as data
parts.what: Problems stored with the elements involved, readable by people, AI and scripts.

parts.name: Warnings panel
parts.what: Lists, filters and zooms to warnings, and offers a fix where one is clear.

features.name: Use phases, options and groups
features.does: Show what is existing, new and demolished, try design options, and repeat sets of elements as groups.

parts.name: Phases
parts.what: Created and demolished phases on every element, with phase filters for views.

parts.name: Design options
parts.what: Option sets and options as fields on elements, with views that choose which option to show.

parts.name: Groups
parts.what: Model and detail groups that repeat a set of elements and update every copy.

parts.name: Assemblies
parts.what: Named sets of elements treated as one item for schedules and shop drawings.

features.name: Stay fast on any size of project
features.does: Open, move around and edit a whole multi-storey building faster than Revit does.

parts.name: Benchmark harness
parts.what: Benchmarks in CI for every target in the map; a regression over 5% blocks the merge.

parts.name: Large test models
parts.what: Anonymised real projects and generated cities used as test fixtures.

parts.name: Truth tests
parts.what: The same element built in Revit and here, compared within tolerance. Revit's geometry comes out through the exporter add-in, which waits on the Revit API terms check (A18-F2-P2).

parts.name: Determinism checks
parts.what: Replays the same log natively and in the browser and requires identical results.

parts.name: Drawing truth tests
parts.what: Plans and sections of the same model compared with Revit's output within a set tolerance: the test behind Gate C.

features.name: Run the same core everywhere
features.does: Run the same model core in the desktop app, in a browser and on a server.

parts.name: Browser core
parts.what: The core compiled to WebAssembly in a web worker, holding only what the person has open.

parts.name: Core to screen protocol
parts.what: A versioned binary protocol: commands in, changes and ready-to-upload geometry chunks out.

parts.name: Headless core service
parts.what: The native core running as a service for AI agents, scripts and multi-user servers.

parts.name: Offline in the browser
parts.what: Small models saved in the browser's own storage, so they open and save with no connection.

areas.name: Geometry kernel and modelling tools
areas.summary: The exact solid geometry under every element, the sketch solver, snapping and editing tools, and massing and free-form shapes.

features.name: Make solid shapes that never break
features.does: Build walls, roofs and components from solids whose cuts and joins always succeed.

parts.name: Solid kernel v1
parts.what: Flat-faced solids on a half-edge structure that always returns a valid solid or a clear error.

parts.name: Booleans
parts.what: Cut, join and intersect ported from Manifold's published method, batched so 300 openings cut as one.

parts.name: Exact predicates
parts.what: Adaptive exact arithmetic for orientation and in-circle tests, so which side of a plane is never wrong.

parts.name: Solid steps
parts.what: Extrude, sweep, revolve, blend and swept blend along lines and arcs.

parts.name: Kernel fuzzing
parts.what: Random solids and boolean sequences; any invalid result is a bug.

parts.name: Tessellation
parts.what: Turns exact solids into meshes split by on-screen error, cached per type and detail level.

parts.name: Kernel start decision
parts.what: A decision note on wrapping Manifold's C++ for the first stretch or writing Rust from day one, with Manifold as the reference answer in tests. One of the six decisions that gate the Design stage; piece A01 studies Manifold's method but does not make this decision.

parts.name: Model tolerance decision
parts.what: A decision note on the one model-wide tolerance (lean: 0.01 mm), set against Revit's short-curve limit of about 0.8 mm.

features.name: Sketch with constraints
features.does: Draw outlines and lock them with dimensions, parallels, equal lengths and alignments.

parts.name: Sketch solver
parts.what: A 2D constraint solver following the planegcs method, written as our own code.

parts.name: Sketch mode
parts.what: Draw lines, arcs, splines, circles and rectangles with snaps and live dimensions.

parts.name: Project locks
parts.what: Locked dimensions and alignments between elements in the project, not only inside families.

parts.name: Project locks decision
parts.what: A decision note on Revit-style locks between elements in the project, or constraints inside families only at first (lean: families first).

features.name: Snap and pick precisely
features.does: Pick and snap to exact ends, middles, centres, intersections and faces.

parts.name: Snapping
parts.what: Snapping against exact kernel geometry, with temporary dimensions while drawing.

parts.name: Picking
parts.what: Fast picking through a GPU ID buffer, with cycling through overlapping elements.

parts.name: Work planes
parts.what: Set a work plane from a level, face, reference plane or line.

parts.name: Measure
parts.what: Measure distances, angles, areas and volumes between picked points, edges and faces, without placing anything.

features.name: Edit elements directly
features.does: Move, copy, rotate, mirror, array, align, offset, trim, split and scale elements.

parts.name: Modify tools
parts.what: The standard modify commands as operations, each with a headless form.

parts.name: Grips and handles
parts.what: Drag ends, shape handles and arrows on screen, with live feedback.

parts.name: Pin and lock
parts.what: Pin elements so nothing moves them by mistake.

parts.name: Paste aligned
parts.what: Paste to the same place, to chosen levels or to chosen views, keeping hosts where they exist.

parts.name: Copy between projects
parts.what: Copy elements with their types between open projects, with a choice when a type of the same name differs.

parts.name: Match type and create similar
parts.what: Give chosen elements another element's type, or start drawing a new element of a picked element's type.

features.name: Mass a building early
features.does: Shape a building as masses, get floor areas from them, and turn mass faces into walls, floors and roofs.

parts.name: Conceptual masses
parts.what: Massing solids with mass floors and gross area reports.

parts.name: Elements from faces
parts.what: Walls, floors and roofs made from mass faces and kept linked. Curtain systems on faces come from A4-F6-P2.

features.name: Model free-form shapes
features.does: Model curved roofs, facades and organic shapes with curved surfaces.

parts.name: Kernel v2 curved surfaces
parts.what: NURBS surfaces and solids behind the same kernel interface.

parts.name: Curved kernel study
parts.what: How OpenCascade and truck handle curved booleans, learning the method only.

parts.name: Adaptive components
parts.what: Point-driven components that repeat across divided surfaces.

parts.name: Subdivision shapes
parts.what: Soft shapes edited by a control cage, then turned into solids.

parts.name: Curved surfaces timing decision
parts.what: A decision note on when curved surfaces become necessary: kernel v1 or v2 (lean: v2).

features.name: Place imported shapes as elements
features.does: Place shapes from other tools as real elements with a category and data.

parts.name: Direct shapes
parts.what: Solids and meshes placed as elements with a category and parameters.

parts.name: Mesh repair
parts.what: Closes holes and fixes normals so imported meshes can be cut and measured.

areas.name: Architectural elements
areas.summary: The building elements an architect models every day. Each is a rule set for how it is shaped, joined, hosted and drawn.

features.name: Set up levels and grids
features.does: Add levels, grids and reference planes, with extents and bubbles set per view.

parts.name: Levels
parts.what: Named datum planes with elevations, storey flags and building ownership.

parts.name: Grids
parts.what: Straight, arc and multi-segment grids with extents set per view.

parts.name: Reference planes
parts.what: Named reference planes for hosting and alignment.

parts.name: Scope boxes
parts.what: Boxes that set the extent of datums and view crops together.

features.name: Draw walls
features.does: Draw layered walls that join cleanly, attach to roofs and floors, and wrap at ends and openings.

parts.name: Wall element
parts.what: Layered wall types with a location line, base and top constraints and attached tops.

parts.name: Wall joins
parts.what: L, T, X and mitre joins solved in plan first, with layer priority and clean-up.

parts.name: Wall profiles and sweeps
parts.what: Edit wall outlines, add sweeps and reveals, and stack walls.

parts.name: Layer wrapping
parts.what: Layers wrap at ends and around inserts by type rules.

features.name: Place doors, windows and openings
features.does: Place doors and windows in walls, and cut shafts and openings through floors and roofs.

parts.name: Hosting
parts.what: Hosted elements store their host and offset and move with the host without rebuilding.

parts.name: Openings and shafts
parts.what: Plain wall openings, shafts through many floors and openings by face.

parts.name: Flip and swap
parts.what: Flip hand and facing, swap types, and keep tags and data.

parts.name: Dormer openings
parts.what: Cut a roof for a dormer from the dormer's walls and roof, kept in step as they move.

features.name: Model floors, ceilings and roofs
features.does: Sketch floors, ceilings and roofs with layers, slopes and edges.

parts.name: Floors
parts.what: Sketched layered floors with slope arrows, shape editing and slab edges.

parts.name: Ceilings
parts.what: Ceilings found from room boundaries or sketched, with grid patterns.

parts.name: Roofs
parts.what: Footprint and extrusion roofs with slopes, soffits, fascias and gutters.

parts.name: Roof solving
parts.what: Solves ridges, hips and valleys and joins between roofs.

features.name: Design stairs, ramps and railings
features.does: Lay out stairs, ramps and railings by rules that check code limits as they are drawn.

parts.name: Stairs
parts.what: Runs, landings and supports laid out by rules, by component or by sketch.

parts.name: Stair code limits
parts.what: Riser, going, pitch and headroom limits per country as data, starting with NZ Building Code clause D1, with the source's terms checked (A24-F1-P6).

parts.name: Railings
parts.what: Railings following paths, with balusters, rails, posts and handrail extensions.

parts.name: Ramps
parts.what: Ramps with slope limits and landings.

features.name: Model curtain walls and glazing
features.does: Draw curtain walls, set their grids and swap panels and mullions.

parts.name: Curtain walls
parts.what: Curtain grids, panels and mullions, with panel sizes driven by the grids.

parts.name: Curtain systems
parts.what: Curtain systems on faces and sloped glazing on roofs.

parts.name: Doors in curtain walls
parts.what: Doors and windows placed as curtain panels.

features.name: Find rooms and areas
features.does: Place rooms that find their own boundaries, and measure areas the way each country's rules ask.

parts.name: Rooms
parts.what: Room boundaries from bounding elements and separation lines, with area, perimeter and volume.

parts.name: Area plans
parts.what: Gross, rentable and custom area schemes with boundary rules per scheme.

parts.name: Area measurement standards
parts.what: Which measurement rules each country uses and how to set them as data, with sources.

parts.name: Colour fills
parts.what: Rooms and areas coloured by a parameter, with a legend. The same colour scheme engine colours any element by value in A20-F6-P1.

features.name: Place furniture, fittings and equipment
features.does: Place furniture, joinery, fixtures and equipment from the library.

parts.name: Placed components
parts.what: Placed instances of family types, hosted or free.

parts.name: Joinery runs
parts.what: Kitchen and joinery runs laid out along a wall from a spec.

features.name: Add model text, lines and parts
features.does: Add 3D text and model lines, and break layered walls and floors into parts.

parts.name: Model text and lines
parts.what: 3D text and model lines as elements.

parts.name: Parts
parts.what: Layered walls and floors broken into parts that can be split, shown and scheduled.

features.name: Show existing and demolished work
features.does: Model an existing building, mark what is demolished and show each phase in its own style.

parts.name: Demolition tools
parts.what: Demolish whole elements, or split off and demolish only the removed piece.

parts.name: Phase graphics
parts.what: Existing, new, demolished and temporary styles per view.

areas.name: Structure
areas.summary: Structural elements, the analytical model and links to analysis software, so engineers work in the same model as the architect.

features.name: Place columns, beams and bracing
features.does: Place columns, beams, bracing and trusses that join and cut back correctly.

parts.name: Structural columns
parts.what: Vertical and slanted columns between levels, attached to beams and floors.

parts.name: Beams and bracing
parts.what: Beams, beam systems and bracing with cut-backs, justification and joins.

parts.name: Trusses
parts.what: Trusses laid out from a profile and member types.

parts.name: Section libraries
parts.what: Steel, timber and concrete section sizes per country as data, from sources whose terms are checked first (A24-F1-P6).

parts.name: Discipline order decision
parts.what: A decision note on which discipline follows the core, structure or services (lean: structure, which has fewer element types).

features.name: Lay out structure from grids
features.does: Place columns at grid crossings and beams along grids in one step.

parts.name: Structure by grid
parts.what: Places columns and beams on chosen grid lines and levels.

features.name: Model foundations and slabs
features.does: Model footings, piles, slabs and retaining walls, and draw the foundation plan a house consent needs.

parts.name: Foundations
parts.what: Isolated, strip and pile foundations hosted to walls, and to structural columns once they arrive (A5-F1-P1).

parts.name: Structural floors and walls
parts.what: Structural use on floors and walls, with span direction and core layers.

parts.name: House foundations to NZS 3604
parts.what: Piles, foundation walls and slab-on-ground edges and thickenings laid out by NZS 3604 rules, with a foundation plan view template.

features.name: Keep an analytical model
features.does: Keep a linked analytical model with nodes, members, panels, supports and loads.

parts.name: Analytical model
parts.what: Analytical members and panels linked to physical elements, kept in step by regeneration.

parts.name: Loads and combinations
parts.what: Point, line and area loads, load cases and combinations per country's loading standard.

parts.name: Supports and releases
parts.what: Boundary conditions and end releases on analytical members.

features.name: Send to analysis and bring results back
features.does: Send the analytical model to analysis software and see results back in the model.

parts.name: Analysis export
parts.what: Exports the analytical model in open formats such as the structural parts of IFC.

parts.name: Analysis links
parts.what: Links to analysis programs through their published formats or APIs, with their terms checked first (A24-F1-P7).

parts.name: Results in the model
parts.what: Forces, deflections and use ratios shown as colours and tags.

features.name: Detail reinforcement
features.does: Place rebar, mesh and cover in concrete, and get bending schedules.

parts.name: Rebar
parts.what: Rebar shapes, sets and mesh hosted in concrete, with cover and hooks, including along 3D paths.

parts.name: Shape codes
parts.what: Bending shape codes per country's standard as data, with the standard's terms checked first (A24-F1-P6).

parts.name: Bending schedules
parts.what: Bending schedules and cut lists from placed rebar.

features.name: Detail steel connections
features.does: Add connections, plates, bolts and welds to steel framing.

parts.name: Connections
parts.what: Parametric connection recipes for common joints.

parts.name: Steel fabrication output
parts.what: Shop drawings and part lists for fabricators, in open steel exchange formats.

areas.name: Building services
areas.summary: Ducts, pipes, cable trays, electrical circuits and their systems, with sizing and calculations, in the same model as the building.

features.name: Route ducts and pipes
features.does: Draw ducts and pipes that add their own fittings at bends, tees and size changes.

parts.name: Ducts
parts.what: Round, rectangular and oval ducts with insulation and lining.

parts.name: Pipes
parts.what: Pipes with slope, insulation and sizes by material.

parts.name: Automatic fittings
parts.what: Routing preferences that choose fittings and sizes as ducts and pipes are drawn.

parts.name: Connectors
parts.what: Typed connectors on families that join to ducts, pipes, conduits and circuits.

parts.name: Route suggestions
parts.what: Suggests routes between connectors that avoid structure and clashes.

parts.name: Flexible ducts and pipes
parts.what: Flexible ducts and pipes that follow a drawn path, with their own pressure loss.

parts.name: Placeholder runs
parts.what: Single-line duct and pipe placeholders for early design that turn into full ducts and pipes with fittings later.

features.name: Build systems
features.does: Group equipment and terminals into systems and see flow and direction.

parts.name: Systems
parts.what: Supply, return, exhaust, water, waste and other systems with flow direction.

parts.name: System browser
parts.what: A tree of systems that shows what is not connected.

parts.name: Gas and hot water

assess: Does the core set produce a full council set for a house (roadmap Gate D), and is anything in it that a house set does not need?
Could someone open the demo and do a whole day's work they do in Revit today: model, document, schedule, sheet and issue, without hitting a gap?
Which add-ins does our own office pay for today, and does each one appear here as a feature with a priority that matches how much we use it?
Is clash, multi-user sync and version compare right as "next", or does a real office need one of them in the first release?
Are the kernel, regeneration graph, hidden line and sketch solver parts sized realistically, and do their work-board pieces (A01, A03, A11, A12) cover the research they need first?
Does every part that reads another company's format or data have a legal part in front of it (Revit exporter terms, direct .rvt reading, DWG, families, standards tables, classification tables)?
Is the Revit exporter add-in the right way in for a first release, and is moving from Revit easy enough that an office would switch?
Are New Zealand rules (D1 stairs, H1 energy, G13 drainage, NZS 3604, height in relation to boundary, LINZ data) covered first, and is the country pack design ready for Australia and others?
Can a person with a disability use the panels and views, and can someone use the app fully offline with no account?
Is every running cost (hosting, cloud rendering, AI use) paid at cost through the kit and shown on the open cost ledger, with what stays free clearly published?
Is the demo's interface our own design, with our own names and icons, and nothing that copies another product's look?
Which parts can start now in the Mapping stage as research and decision notes, and which must wait for the first six decisions?
Are there features missing that a structural engineer, a services engineer, a builder or a council officer would expect to see?
Do the parts lean on the shared kit and engines where they should, rather than building their own accounts, payments, messaging or PDF output?
Has the kit made core the two parts Spare Construct's first release needs (its plugin host KIT-A16-F5-P2 and chunked storage KIT-A15-F6-P2), or should Spare Construct's first release wait for them?
Does the house consent checklist (CON-A11-F5-P4) match what councils ask for, and are the items it marks as coming from outside acceptable at Gate D?

Do the decisions that gate the Design stage but have no work-board piece yet (storage layout CON-A2-F4-P8, kernel start CON-A3-F1-P7) now have pieces, and does every other decision part have one before its build part starts?
